top_global_features.label: Built-Up Density
top_global_features.reason: Dense built-up surfaces reduce natural ground absorption and increase runoff potential.

top_global_features.label: 24h Rainfall
top_global_features.reason: Higher 24-hour rainfall represents the total volume of water accumulated over the day.

top_global_features.label: 6h Rainfall
top_global_features.reason: 6-hour rainfall volume indicates mid-term precipitation intensity and storm duration.

top_global_features.label: Elevation
top_global_features.reason: Elevation determines natural drainage paths and low-lying accumulation zones.

top_global_features.label: Slope
top_global_features.reason: Flatter slopes slow down natural drainage, leading to surface water pooling.

top_global_features.label: 1h Rainfall
top_global_features.reason: 1-hour rainfall volume captures short-duration peak precipitation intensity.

top_global_features.label: Antecedent Rainfall Proxy
top_global_features.reason: Rainfall from previous days limits the remaining ground absorption capacity.

top_global_features.label: Low Slope Risk
top_global_features.reason: Identifies areas with flat terrain highly susceptible to water accumulation.

top_global_features.label: 3h Rainfall
top_global_features.reason: 3-hour rainfall volume contributes to short-to-mid-term runoff generation.

top_global_features.label: Built-Up Density and Low Vegetation Interaction
top_global_features.reason: Interaction between dense building cover and lack of vegetation accelerates runoff.

known_limitations: Target variable is an engineered index, not direct flood sensor readings.
Trained using weak labels based on a combined exposure-hazard formula.
Does not account for real-time drainage network updates or blockages.
honesty_note: The model predicts an engineered weather-impact risk score derived from real weather, satellite, road, and exposure features. It is not trained on verified official flood incident labels.
